# Universal Memory Protocol (UMP)

> UMP is an open standard for agent memory. What MCP did for tools, UMP does for memory: one portable record format, one small operation set, and bindings that work across agents, runtimes, and storage engines.

## What is UMP?

Universal Memory Protocol (universalmemoryprotocol.io) standardises how agents read, write, revise, forget, and exchange memory. It is not a database and not a single memory product. It is a small protocol surface, a portable signed record format, and reference SDK and server code that any agent harness or memory backend can implement.

You may already have useful memories in agent files, Claude or Codex project notes, Recall exports, Obsidian folders, Postgres, Redis, SQLite, or a vector database. UMP turns those into one portable memory shape so new agents and new stores extend the same memory instead of starting over.

- Site: https://universalmemoryprotocol.io
- Source: https://github.com/edihasaj/universal-memory-protocol
- Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@universalmemoryprotocol/core
- Status: live v0.1

## Bindings

MCP, HTTP, and file export. Add persistent UMP memory to any MCP host:

```jsonc
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ump": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@universalmemoryprotocol/core", "ump-memory"] }
  }
}
```
